text:
noah (ACME): Hi team — since the plan migration at ~09:15 PST our app on the dedicated-west-1 pool is getting 429s and elevated tail latency. Can someone look?

ashley (Support): Sorry you're hitting this, noah. Can you share tenant id + sample request/response headers? We'll pull logs.

noah (ACME): Tenant T-ACME-42. Sample response: `HTTP/1.1 429` body: `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded"}`. Headers: `x-tenant-quota: 10`, `x-tenant-remaining: 0`, `x-request-id: r-9a1b`. Requests peaked ~600 r/s.

kevin (SRE): Thanks — tagging infra. Two quick checks: 1) confirm quota mapping after migration; 2) confirm autoscaler decision path. Can infra fetch quota config: `GET /internal/quotas?tenant=T-ACME-42` and paste output.

maria (Infra): Pasted output from quota-service:```json
{
  "tenant_id": "T-ACME-42",
  "plan": "enterprise",
  "quota_units": 10,
  "pool": "dedicated-west-1"
}```This looks wrong — expected ~1000 units for enterprise dedicated. The migration job appears to have applied the public-tier multiplier (x1) instead of dedicated multiplier (x100).

james (Eng): Confirming: the plan migrate script uses mapPlanToUnits(plan) but we forgot to pass pool_type. For dedicated pools we multiply units by `dedicated_multiplier`. If that wasn't applied, tenants end up with tiny per-second budgets and hit token bucket drain -> 429s.

kevin (SRE): That would also explain autoscaler behaviour: autoscaler includes a quota check `if quota_units_remaining < scale_threshold then skip_scale_up` to avoid scaling for tenants limited by billing policy. With quota_units = 10, it never triggers scale. So both throttling and lack of autoscale are symptoms of the same mapping bug.

ashley (Support): Possible mitigations: 1) manual quota bump for T-ACME-42 via admin API; 2) emergency rollback of migration mapping; 3) patch migration job and re-run for affected tenants. Which should we do now?

maria (Infra): I'm doing a manual bump now: `POST /admin/tenants/T-ACME-42/quota -d '{"quota_units":1000}'` — applying.

ops-bot: Incident created: #incidents/2120001111-dedicated-quota-migration by maria

noah (ACME): Re-testing now… good sign, initial requests return 200s and latency looks back to normal. Thanks.

ashley (Support): Great — can you confirm traffic for 10m to be sure? We'll keep a close eye and escalate if it resurfacing.

noah (ACME): Running load test — 15m steady at 600 r/s, no 429s in the last 6m. Will update if anything else.

james (Eng): Follow-ups: 1) patch migration to include `pool_type` in mapping (PR in progress), 2) add a post-migration validation check that flags `quota_units` < expected_for_plan, 3) run backfill for all dedicated pools to recalc units. I'll open the PR and link here.

kevin (SRE): Also logging item: autoscaler logic should not permanently skip scale-up solely on a per-tenant quota that appears to be misconfigured. Add a safety path to allow a single emergency scale if request queue > X. I'll file a backlog ticket.

maria (Infra): For the immediate set, I patched 3 tenants that showed the same issue. I'll run a sweep script over dedicated-* and output findings.

ashley (Support): Thanks everyone. noah — sorry for the disruption. We'll follow up with a brief incident summary and the action items.

noah (ACME): Thanks team — appreciate the fast turnaround :thumbsup:
